title: Eleven Weeks
logline: A public health midwife's rounds through a dry-zone village follow several pregnancies at once, each body being assembled week by week, out of sight of everyone but its mother.
human_question: Before a person has a name, a face, or lungs of their own, what is already being built?

premise.story: A working round of home visits by a rural midwife over several weeks, following two or three expectant mothers at different stages, told through their own care and concerns.
premise.place: Scattered village households and a small rural clinic in the dry zone.
premise.experience: Travelling between houses on a motorbike or bicycle, weighing and checking, quiet advice about food and rest, and a family's own preparations for a birth.

concept_links.why: The source traces exactly this: matter assembling from a first speck through named weekly stages, fed by warmth, mind and food arriving in a fixed order, through the mother's own nourishment. The midwife's rounds are the everyday care that surrounds that unseen process.
Growth and continuity, named among the non-concrete kinds of matter, are the visible register of that week-by-week assembly, most concretely observable in a pregnancy followed over time.

what_camera_could_observe: Mothers being weighed and checked, quiet advice given
Paperwork and records kept for each pregnancy
Families preparing rooms, clothes or ceremonies for a coming birth
A due date approaching, and whatever the family and clinic decide to share
what_must_be_real: Full informed consent from mothers and their families at every stage. No staged examinations, no medical claims presented as advice, and the doctrine's weekly stages never set against or confused with real medical guidance.

possible_arc.ending_open: A birth, if the family and hospital agree to include it, or the film ending before that point out of respect for privacy.

requirements: A rural public health midwife willing to have her rounds filmed
Expectant mothers and families giving full, ongoing consent

suggestions.name: Rural villages served by a public health midwife
suggestions.why: A well-known dry-zone agricultural region with an established rural public health midwife service.
suggestions.verify: A specific midwife, clinic and willing families are unverified.

risks: Pregnancy is private and medically sensitive; consent must be ongoing and revocable at every stage
The doctrine's weekly stages must never be presented as medical fact or set against real medical advice
Mothers must control what is filmed and shown, especially near a birth
drop_if: No midwife or expectant mothers willing to participate
Hospital or ministry permissions are unavailable

connections.note: A body assembled week by week in one film; the same body, years later, taught to take itself apart again, part by part, in the next.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
